sourceReview: The guard resolves each dependency through its original scan owner and original exact member identity, then checks the selected descriptor availability is exactly required. It does not infer availability from logicalType.nullable.

The shared dependency traversal covers both sides of equality, every lexicographic column and Field value, every join/filter/group/order dependency, SUM arguments, and HasRelated terminal authored Key fields. Plain Field outputs receive a separate pass.

Same-named Fields in different Records resolve by owner and qualified identity. The independent controls include required Other.token alongside optional Resource.token and both accepted/refused owner-sensitive queries.

HasRelated Field-valued key operands already refuse in application_scope; original authored_key uses scalar_type, which requires required availability. Terminal-key handling was source-reviewed, not a newly executed terminal-key test.
Field-free COUNT retains the original scan without selecting unrelated members. Unselected optional Fields do not cause blanket refusal. Required SUM still retains unsupported property semantics.

Both current application_lineage and legacy security_query_properties call the common guard before returning their report. Refusals produce the intended WFT-APPLICATION-LINEAGE-AVAILABILITY prefix and no partial stdout in the executed cases.

resolvedDefect.description: The old selected report profile admitted absent-allowed Fields with ideal nullable:false property uses and no separate use availability. The full retained applicationPlanJson could still contain descriptor availability; this is not a claim that every retained source archive erased it. The fix refuses that unrepresented selected meaning.
